clue.text: Boil and give devilled crab to relative

indicators.note: devilled food is spiced and stirred up, so the letters of the next word get rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, ready to be rearranged
an uncle is a family relative

explanation.surface: A cook makes a peppery crab dish and serves it to a family member.
explanation.definitionFit: A carbuncle is a large painful boil or abscess under the skin, so the words are synonyms.

clue.text: Animal arrived at lake

parts.note: came to a place means arrived at it
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A creature turns up at the water's edge.
explanation.definitionFit: A camel is a humped desert beast, one example of the general class named.

clue.text: Rebel artist knocking back litre of acid

parts.note: RA, Royal Academician, is the stock abbreviation for an artist

indicators.note: knocking something back turns it round, so the phrase after it is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: L is the symbol for litre
taken as written

explanation.surface: A rebellious painter downs a litre of LSD in one go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knocking back' sounds like drinking, but it turns 'litre of acid' round as a unit.
explanation.definitionFit: A radical is a revolutionary person pushing for extreme political change, close in sense to a rebel.

clue.text: Funny guy hanging round student is loathsome

indicators.note: something hanging round another thing surrounds it on both sides
funny here means odd or peculiar, so the word after it is jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged
L, the learner plate, stands for a student

explanation.surface: A comedian who loiters around a student is detestable.
explanation.definitionFit: Ugly can mean repulsive or unpleasant in conduct as well as in looks, matching hateful.

clue.text: Note: wood for kind of shoe

parts.note: C is one of the musical notes
a log is a piece of wood

explanation.surface: A memo reminding someone that timber is used to make footwear.
explanation.definitionFit: A clog is a heavy wooden-soled shoe, a specific style of footwear.

clue.text: This starship is the business

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the spaceship captained by Kirk in Star Trek
second meaning: a commercial firm or venture

explanation.surface: A boast that this spaceship is the very best there is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The business' reads as slang for excellent, but it is literally a company.
explanation.definitionFit: The USS Enterprise is the Star Trek vessel, and an enterprise is also a commercial undertaking or company.

clue.text: In winter plough an area in West Africa

definitions.note: stands for the country found there

indicators.note: in signals that the letters sit inside the following words, spanning their boundaries

parts.note: the letters run across the end of plough, all of an and the start of area

explanation.surface: A farmer turns over a field during the cold season somewhere in West Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: A loose Quiptic clue: 'winter' is surface padding, and the definition is the location phrase 'in West Africa'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ghana is a nation on the Gulf of Guinea coast, located in western Africa.

clue.text: Sociable Mr Dyke takes us round a city in Brazil

parts.note: Greg Dyke was the BBC's director-general at the time
taken as written
Rio de Janeiro
taken as written

explanation.surface: A friendly broadcasting boss takes his colleagues on a tour of Rio.
explanation.walkthrough: Greg Dyke was director-general of the BBC around 2000. The pieces simply follow one another.
explanation.definitionFit: Gregarious describes someone who enjoys company and mixing with others, a synonym of outgoing.

clue.text: Worry is easing love out

indicators.note: out can mean wrong or disordered, so the letters before it are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
love is zero in tennis, which looks like O

explanation.surface: Anxiety fades as romance leaves a relationship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out' looks like love departing, but it tells you to scramble the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To agonise is to fret or torment oneself over something, the verb sense of worry.

clue.text: Spoke to a churchman about journalist on a ship

indicators.note: in a down entry one thing sitting on another is placed above it, so the piece named after this word goes first

parts.note: taken as written
DD, Doctor of Divinity, is a clergyman's qualification
re means concerning or about
SS stands for steamship
ED is short for editor

explanation.surface: Someone talked to a priest about a reporter aboard a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Addressed a person means directed speech to them, a synonym of talked to.

clue.text: The white line to follow is safe but boring

definitions.meaning: first meaning, literal: where the centre markings are painted

explanation.surface: Driving advice: keep to the painted lane marking, which is safe but dull.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally the centre of a carriageway, and figuratively a cautious, middling, unexciting position or taste.

clue.text: Want the French to take a hundred thousand

parts.note: la is French for the (feminine)
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
K stands for a thousand, as in 10K

explanation.surface: The French wish to accept a sum of a hundred thousand.
explanation.definitionFit: Want as a noun means a shortage or absence, which is what a deficiency is.

clue.text: Arrange wild orgies with headless man involved

indicators.note: a headless word has lost its first letter
something involved is taken inside, so one piece is wrapped by the other
wild means out of control, so the word after it is scrambled

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged
man without its first letter

explanation.surface: Plan some riotous parties with a beheaded man in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: To organise is to put things in order or set up an event, a synonym of arrange.

clue.text: He can deal with those who are late

definitions.text: He can deal with those who are late

parts.words: He can deal with those who are late
parts.note: surface reading: someone who handles latecomers, like a teacher or receptionist
setter's reading: late means deceased, so this is the person who arranges funerals

explanation.surface: Someone whose job is handling people who turn up behind time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Late' as in 'the late Mr Smith' means dead, not tardy.
explanation.definitionFit: A funeral director prepares the dead and organises burials, so this is the professional who deals with the deceased.

clue.text: Weather systems to cause chilled faces

definitions.meaning: first meaning: boundaries where cooler air masses advance
second meaning, read literally: fronts that are cold

explanation.surface: Meteorological patterns that leave people with frozen cheeks.
explanation.definitionFit: Meteorologists name the leading edges of cooler air masses this, and a front is also a face or facade.

clue.text: Southern friend losing heart gets to destroy our luxury

indicators.note: losing its heart means the middle letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for southern
pal, a friend, with its central letter removed
to end something is to finish or destroy it
taken as written

explanation.surface: A dispirited Southern pal sets about wrecking our lavish lifestyle.
explanation.definitionFit: Splendour is magnificence or lavish richness, close in meaning to opulence.

clue.text: So quiet or, if in charge, sleep inducing

parts.note: taken as written
p, piano, is the musical direction for quiet
taken as written
taken as written
i/c is the usual short form of in charge

explanation.surface: A sarcastic remark that a hushed person in authority would be dull enough to send you off.
explanation.definitionFit: A soporific drug or speech makes people drowsy, the meaning of causing slumber.

clue.text: The Times ruined news stories

indicators.note: something ruined is wrecked, so the word before it is broken up and rebuilt

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A complaint that a famous newspaper has spoiled its reporting.
explanation.walkthrough: The Times is a London daily newspaper, which makes the reporting surface natural.
explanation.definitionFit: Items are individual pieces of reporting in a paper or bulletin, so they are reports.

clue.text: Pounding back up to the London School of Economics

indicators.note: back means the following word is turned round to read the other way

parts.note: taken as written
the usual initials of the university college

explanation.surface: Someone races back to the university with a thumping heart.
explanation.definitionFit: A pulse is the rhythmic throbbing of blood in the arteries, a regular beating.

clue.text: Lion with father on the way to becoming a different cat

parts.note: Leo is the lion of the zodiac
pa is a familiar word for dad
RD is the abbreviation for road

explanation.surface: A lion and its sire set off to turn into another species of feline.
explanation.definitionFit: The leopard is a spotted big cat, a separate species from the lion.

clue.text: Mentally ill doctor died with burst inside

indicators.note: inside places one piece within the other, splitting the outer word

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the word it governs is reworked

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A medic dies after something ruptures within him, leaving people in shock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like a noun (DR), but it is a verb telling you to rearrange burst.
explanation.definitionFit: Disturbed describes someone with a psychiatric or emotional disorder, so unwell in the mind.

clue.text: Ma, Bob 'n I are messing around with the baby

indicators.note: messing around means fooling about in disorder, so the letters named before are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
the shortened and
taken as written

explanation.surface: A family plays about with the infant.
explanation.definitionFit: Bambino is Italian for a little child, used in English for an infant.

clue.text: Cocks include duck in duty rotas

indicators.note: to include something is to take it inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: rosters are lists of who works when
a duck is a score of nought in cricket, shaped like O

explanation.surface: Farmyard birds are added to the chore schedules.
explanation.definitionFit: Roosters are male domestic fowl, which is what cocks are.

clue.text: I'm inside to back up and delete

indicators.note: in an across clue back up means the combined result is turned round to run the other way
inside puts the first piece within the second

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A computer instruction: put me inside, make a backup and delete.
explanation.definitionFit: To omit is to leave out or remove, a synonym of striking or deleting.

clue.text: Idea contained in the metaphor

indicators.note: contained in means the letters are held inside the following words

parts.note: the letters run across the whole of the and the start of metaphor

explanation.surface: A literary concept lies within a figure of speech.
explanation.definitionFit: A theme is a central subject or underlying notion of a work, close to an idea.

clue.text: Captain standing on his head must be a warning!

indicators.note: in a down entry, turning upside down means the name is read from bottom to top

parts.note: Captain Nemo commands the Nautilus in Jules Verne's novel

explanation.surface: A captain doing a headstand must signal trouble ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: An omen is a sign of what is to come, usually foreboding, so a portent or warning.

clue.text: Case all about winners

indicators.note: all about suggests letters scattered in every direction, so they are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A legal case concerns those who came first.
explanation.definitionFit: Aces are top performers or unreturnable tennis serves, both kinds of champions or point-winning shots.

clue.text: With this, letters need no stamps, since Monsieur is playing with French ink again

definitions.text: With this, letters need no stamps

indicators.note: playing with things means fiddling about, so the letters that follow are rearranged

parts.note: M is the French abbreviation for Monsieur
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Frenchman fiddles with his ink once more, explaining why his post needs no stamps.
explanation.definitionFit: An office device prints postage marks on envelopes, replacing adhesive stamps on mail.

clue.text: Drink with Rosie

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an alcoholic apple drink

definitions.note: a fill-in-the-blank: the word completes a book title
definitions.meaning: second meaning: completes Laurie Lee's memoir of a Cotswold childhood

explanation.walkthrough: Laurie Lee's 1959 memoir of village life in Gloucestershire is a classic of English schooldays reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Fermented apple juice is the beverage, and it also opens the title Cider with Rosie.

clue.text: Smooths down modulation on soft rock

parts.note: to sand wood is to smooth it with abrasive paper
tone is the pitch or inflection of a voice

explanation.surface: A producer smooths out the vocal inflections on a gentle rock track.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soft rock' looks like a music genre but is a literal geology term.
explanation.definitionFit: Sandstone is a sedimentary stone made of compacted grains, relatively crumbly compared with granite.
